Task: Deduplicate Attachment Cleanup in Cronjob & Prevent Out-of-Bounds Panics

  • Area: Cronjob / Attachments / Deduplication / Crash Prevention
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/CleanFileAttachments.go
    • src/Action/V1/Cronjob/cronjob_safety_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-29

1. Problem & Context

In src/Action/V1/Cronjob/CleanFileAttachments.go, cleaning bug attachments (/attachments/b/) and contact form attachments (/attachments/c/) duplicated 45 lines of identical logic verbatim:

  • Querying directory files with filepath.Glob.
  • Splitting strings by subdirectory marker (b/ vs c/).
  • Slicing dates: subParts[0][0:4], [4:6], [6:8].
  • Comparing age >= 2 days and deleting with os.Remove.
    Additionally, direct slicing subParts[0][0:4] without checking string length caused an immediate index out of range runtime panic on non-conforming or short filenames.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Centralized Helper Function (CleanFileAttachments.go):
    • Implemented cleanAttachmentSubDir(dirPath, marker string).
    • Encapsulates file traversal, timestamp parsing, age comparison (daysLeft >= 2), and safe deletion.
    • Preserves 100% of existing fmt.Println monitoring logs, flow sequence, and return values.
  2. Bounds Safety Guard:
    • Added len(subParts[0]) >= 8 guard before date substring extraction to prevent out-of-range crashes on short filenames.
  3. Zero Configuration & Zero Contract Changes:
    • No new environment variables added; execution flow and outputs remain 100% identical.
  4. Unit Testing:
    • Added TestCleanFileAttachments_MissingDir_ReturnsNil and TestCleanAttachmentSubDir_HandlesShortFilenamesWithoutPanic in cronjob_safety_test.go.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • 45+ lines of duplicate cleanup code eliminated.
  • Out-of-bounds panics on short attachment filenames are prevented.
  • All existing fmt.Println log outputs and behavior remain 100% identical.
  • 100% unit tests pass in src/Action/V1/Cronjob.
  • Clean build and vet checks.

issues.display_title: Issue #580: Defensive Nil-Pointer Guards and Socket Leak Prevention in Elasticsearch Utilities
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Defensive Nil-Pointer Guards and Socket Leak Prevention in Elasticsearch Utilities

  • Date: 2026-10-30
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS
  • Configuration: ZERO NEW ENV REQUIRED

1. Summary

Hardened all Elasticsearch connectors, counter managers, and retrieval utilities against nil pointer dereferences and socket resource leaks:

  1. Eliminated Nil Fiber Context Panics:

    • Secured RetrieveElastic and RetrieveElasticV1 against crashes when c == nil by guarding c.Status(...) calls on missing _source.
    • Added nil checks on elasticClient and response objects across all operations.

  2. Prevented Socket / Connection Leaks:

    • Ensured res.Body.Close() is always called conditionally and safely in CheckElasticExist, DeleteElastic, DeleteCounterFollowerFollowingPosts, and SetDocument.

  3. Subpackage Hardening:

    • ElasticPost: Guarded nil DB and nil client across all 5 counter functions.
    • ElasticComment: Guarded nil client and nil DB across all 3 counter functions; removed fmt.Println debug noise.
    • ElasticBookmark: Guarded nil DB and nil client across 3 functions.
    • ElasticUsers: Guarded nil DB and nil client across 4 functions.
    • ElasticNotForPublic: Guarded nil DB and nil client in AddCounterReplyCommentPost.

  4. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Created nil_safety_test.go across ElasticSearch, ElasticPost, ElasticComment, ElasticBookmark, and ElasticUsers.

Task: Defensive Nil-Pointer Guards and Socket Leak Prevention in Elasticsearch Utilities

  • Area: Elasticsearch / Crash Prevention / Reliability / Resource Management
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticPost/ElasticPost.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticComment/ElasticComment.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticBookmark/ElasticBookmark.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticUsers/ElasticUsers.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticNotForPublic/ElasticNotForPublic.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/nil_safety_test.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticPost/nil_safety_test.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticComment/nil_safety_test.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticBookmark/nil_safety_test.go
    • src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticUsers/nil_safety_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-30

1. Problem & Context

  1. Critical Panic on Nil Fiber Context in RetrieveElastic & RetrieveElasticV1:
    When _source was not found in the Elasticsearch response, RetrieveElastic and RetrieveElasticV1 called c.Status(fiber.StatusInternalServerError).JSON(...) directly. Multiple callers (cronjobs such as UpdateScoreTimeline.go, UpdateRecommendationScores.go, and internal helpers in ElasticPost, ElasticComment, and ElasticUsers) pass c == nil. This caused an immediate runtime nil pointer dereference panic, crashing background tasks and worker routines.
  2. Missing Nil Checks on Elasticsearch Client and DB:
    Functions in ElasticPost, ElasticComment, ElasticBookmark, ElasticUsers, and ElasticSearch (GetCounterValue, SetDocument, CheckElasticExist, DeleteCounterFollowerFollowingPosts) lacked defensive guards for uninitialized Config.DB or nil Elasticsearch clients.
  3. Socket/Connection Leaks:
    CheckElasticExist failed to close res.Body, leaking HTTP connections upon each existence check.
  4. Log Noise:
    Raw fmt.Println debug statements were present in ElasticComment.AddCounterReplyComment.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Nil Fiber Context Defense (src/Utils/ElasticSearch/ElasticSearch.go):
    • Added if c != nil check before invoking c.Status(...).JSON(...) on missing _source. When c == nil, returns nil, errors.New("source not found in elasticsearch response").
    • Added guards for elasticClient == nil in RetrieveElastic, RetrieveElasticV1, SetDocument, CheckElasticExist, and DeleteElastic.
    • Ensured safe body closing (if res != nil && res.Body != nil { defer res.Body.Close() }) across all request executions, preventing connection leaks.
  2. Defensive Guards for DB & Client Across Subpackages:
    • ElasticPost: Guarded against nil Config.DB and nil elastic client in AddCounterCommentPost, AddCounterLikePost, AddCounterViewsPost, AddCounterPostV1, and SetCounterCommentPostForBan.
    • ElasticComment: Guarded against nil connElastic and nil Config.DB in AddCounterLikeComment, AddCounterReplyComment, and SetCounterReplyCommentForBan. Removed raw debug logging.
    • ElasticBookmark: Guarded against nil Config.DB and nil elastic in AddCounterTotalBookmarks, AddCounterTotalBookmarksV1, and SetCounterTotalBookmarksForBan.
    • ElasticUsers: Guarded against nil Config.DB and nil elastic in AddCounterFollowerFollowingPosts, AddCounterTotalPosts, AddCounterProfileUser, and AddCounterFollowerFollowing.
    • ElasticNotForPublic: Guarded against nil Config.DB and nil elastic in AddCounterReplyCommentPost.
  3. Zero Configuration & Zero Breaking Changes:
    • ZERO new environment variables required.
    • All method signatures and return formats remain 100% backward compatible.
  4. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Created test suites verifying nil client and nil DB safety across all Elasticsearch packages.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • Background workers and cronjobs passing c == nil will never panic on missing Elasticsearch documents.
  • Nil database and client dereferences are safely handled with clean error propagation.
  • HTTP response bodies are safely closed, eliminating socket leaks.
  • 100% unit tests pass across all packages (go test ./...).
  • Clean go vet and go build ./cmd/... checks.

  • Date: 2026-10-30

1. Summary

Enforced ACID transaction atomicity across core panorama post publishing and video update handlers:

  1. Transactional Multi-Panorama Updates (src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostComplete.go):

    • Pre-computed panorama settings (sequence, animation, little_planet, filter, default_thumb) into in-memory slice multiUpdates.

Task: Enforce ACID Transaction Atomicity on Core Post Publishing and Video Update

  • Area: Posts / Data Integrity / Transactions / ACID / Reliability
  • Files Affected:
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/AddPostComplete.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/UpdatePostVideo.go
    • src/Action/V1/Posts/post_update_transaction_test.go
  • Date: 2026-10-30

1. Problem & Context

  1. Non-Atomic Multi-Panorama Publishing in AddPostComplete.go:
    When completing/publishing a multiple-panorama post, the handler performed sequential updates to each record in the multiple_post table inside a loop, followed by an update to the parent record in posts. If any panorama update failed midway (e.g. invalid sequence, constraint violation, or connection drop), previously updated panoramas were committed to the database while the parent post was not published, leaving the post in a corrupt, inconsistent state.
  2. Disconnected DB Calls in UpdatePostVideo.go:
    Updating 360 video posts executed updates to little_planet_filter and posts across separate database calls without an atomic boundary. A failure in the post update left modified filter parameters committed without updating post metadata or visibility.

2. Scope & Solution

  1. Atomic Transaction in AddPostComplete.go:
    • Pre-computed all panorama updates in memory into multiUpdates.
    • Wrapped the loop of multiple_post updates and the parent posts update inside Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }).
    • Guaranteed all-or-nothing execution: any failure immediately triggers automatic rollback, leaving database state clean.
    • Preserved exact legacy error messages and status codes:
      • MultiplePost error -> 400 Bad Request with "Update Multiple Post Failed"
      • Post error -> 400 Bad Request with "Update Post Complete Failed"
  2. Atomic Transaction in UpdatePostVideo.go:
    • Wrapped conditional little_planet_filter update and parent posts update inside Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Preserved exact legacy error messages and status codes:
      • Filter error -> 400 Bad Request with "Update Filter Failed"
      • Post error -> 400 Bad Request with "Update Post Failed"
  3. Zero Configuration & Zero Breaking Changes:
    • ZERO new environment variables required.
    • All response structures, payloads, and error contracts remain 100% backward compatible.
  4. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Added post_update_transaction_test.go covering authorization gates and required parameters.

3. Acceptance Criteria

  • All database mutations in AddPostComplete and UpdatePostVideo are protected by database transactions.
  • Partial failures roll back cleanly with zero orphaned or desynchronized records.
  • 100% unit tests pass across src/Action/V1/Posts.
  • Clean go vet and go build ./cmd/... checks.
